item.title: The next move on Kings’ radar after Nique Clifford trade
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The next move on Kings’ radar after Nique Clifford trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sacramento Kings are looking to add depth to their backcourt after a difficult start to the season. Their latest Nique Clifford roster move has given them more financial flexibility, and the front office is now considering several options. According to NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer, Sacramento has shown interest in free-agent guards Kevin Porter Jr. and Gabe Vincent as potential backups for rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. The Kings recently agreed to send Clifford to the Oklahoma City Thunder in exchange for two second-round picks. The deal leaves Sacramento approximately $6.4 million below the luxury tax line, with two open standard roster spots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Porter was previously on Sacramento’s radar before the Milwaukee Bucks waived him near the end of the preseason. The 26-year-old averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, and 5.2 rebounds in 38 games last season. Vincent is also available after spending time with the Los Angeles Lakers and Atlanta Hawks, averaging 4.4 points across 53 appearances. The Kings are also considering converting Leaky Black’s two-way contract into a standard deal. He has earned consideration after providing useful minutes while Keegan Murray and De’Andre Hunter deal with injuries. Porter and Vincent would offer different options for Sacramento. Porter brings more scoring and playmaking, while Vincent could provide another experienced guard in the rotation. Neither player has agreed to a deal with the Kings. Sacramento is 1-9 and has several roster decisions to make as it looks for a way forward. The Clifford trade created room for another addition, and finding reliable help behind Acuff appears to be one of the team’s priorities. item.title: Taylor Swift’s mom wore iconic Travis Kelce ‘Karma’ shirt at Chiefs’ win vs. Jets
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images. Taylor Swift’s mom wore iconic Travis Kelce ‘Karma’ shirt at Chiefs’ win vs. Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In Week 9, the Kansas City Chiefs beat the New York Jets, and Travis Kelce ’s wife, Taylor Swift, attended the game with her mom, Andrea. Andrea Swift was wearing a shirt that read, “Karma is the guy on the Chiefs.” Of course, this was a nod to her daughter’s famous lyric change for her song “Karma” on the Eras Tour. 📸 | Andrea Swift wearing a “Karma is the guy on the Chiefs” shirt at today’s Chiefs game pic.twitter.com/YW2YXsTiH2 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Taylor Swift News (@TSwiftNZ) November 8, 2026 They were both extremely happy when the picture was taken. It’s unknown when it was taken, but Kelce had a big game, so it was probably after one of his plays. Taylor Swift’s husband Travis Kelce’s big game in the Chiefs’ win over the Jets Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Kelce was the Chiefs’ leading receiver in their Week 9 win against the Jets, catching four passes for 72 yards, including a long 38-yard catch. He scored a touchdown, but it was counted as a rushing touchdown. This was his first trip to the end zone since Week 3. Over the last few weeks, Kelce has been on fire. He caught five passes for 67 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Denver Broncos. He is on pace to log over 1,000 yards for the first time since 2022. We’ll see if he is able to keep pace. The Chiefs got back on track in Week 9 after losing back-to-back games out of their bye against the Seattle Seahawks and the Broncos. Kenneth Walker III finally looked like his early season self, rushing for 102 yards and also catching four passes for 41 yards and two touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes, who suffered an injury scare during a strip sack, finished the game with 242 yards and two touchdown passes. They will visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10 before hosting the Arizona Cardinals the following week. Then, they will play the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. At 6-2, the Chiefs are still in second place in the AFC West after losing to the Broncos last week. item.title: 2026 Atlanta Braves Player Review: Blake Burkhalter
item.description: If anyone forgot that Blake Burkhalter made an appearance for the Atlanta Braves this season, they likely would not be alone. What he did this season is the definition of the term “cup of coffee” in the majors, one of a handful of players in the Braves organization with the same experience in 2026. How Acquired Blake Burkhalter was drafted by the Braves in the same draft class as JR Ritchie (2022), in the second round, out of Auburn University. He has been in the Braves system ever since. The highest he reached in the prospect rankings in his time was 14th by Baseball America. Somewhat interestingly and/or tellingly, the Braves did not protect Burkhalter by adding him to the 40-man roster ahead of last year’s Rule 5 Draft. This suggests that either they didn’t think highly of him, or figured other teams wouldn’t. They were right, in that no one bothered to claim Burkhalter, and also in that they had little interest in using him at the big league level. What were the expectations? There were virtually no expectations at the MLB level for Burkhalter, and any that existed probably took a hit when he was left unprotected. Beyond hovering around the 40 FV area, Burkhalter had a rough go of it after being promoted to Triple-A in 2025, with an FIP of 4.82 and an xFIP of 5.43 (and an xERA in that same area) while working mostly as a reliever. The presumption was that he’d need to show something in the way of better peripherals before being a candidate for the big league roster. 2026 Results It was a true cup of coffee for Burkhalter. The truest, really. He was promoted to the big leagues when rosters expanded on September 1, he pitched one inning, and then he was sent down the next day. The end. That inning featured one hit, one walk, one strikeout, and one run charged to him. The Braves were already trailing 5-2, and the two baserunners, along with a wild pitch and two flyouts, led to a sixth Nationals run via sacrifice fly. He did at least end on a high note with his strikeout of Daylen Lile. His bigger action was in the minors, where he dealt with some injury stuff and a variety of rehab assignments. Working as a pure reliever in Triple-A, he pitched 29 2/3 innings over 21 appearances, with a 2.43 ERA that was belied by a 3.35 FIP and 4.37 xFIP. He did strike out a bunch of guys (about 27 percent of batters faced), but his walk rate was about as close to being double digits (9.8 percent) as possible without actually tripping that concerning threshold. What went right? What went right is that Burkhalter can now say he was an MLB pitcher. He made his debut and it was not a terrible one, though it wasn’t great either. Beyond that, you can point to his ERA in the minors, where he again outpitched his peripherals substantially. Maybe he’s got some kind of unique ability to do so, but the Braves don’t seem to buy it. item.title: Monday Bantering: Jays Notes
item.description: TORONTO, ON - SEPTEMBER 27: Baseballs sit in a baseball glove during the second inning of an MLB game between the Cincinnati Reds and the Toronto Blue Jays on September 27, 2026, at Rogers Centre in Toronto, ON. (Photo by Mathew Tsang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Back from our week away. Huatulco, Mexico, is a nice area. Not over-developed yet (they are working at it, though). The people in the resorts are largely Canadian (it is hard to fly there from the States, but WestJet has direct flights from many cities). Still, a big topic of conversation was the US election. We mostly stayed at the resort, ate and drank too much. We did take an outing to a cemetery for the Day of the Dead. It is a really nice idea, a day (really a week) for people to think about, talk about, loved ones who have passed. People dress up and dress up the grave sites. I talked for a couple of minutes to a fellow whose young son was buried there, and he seemed happy to have the chance to talk about him. I want to borrow the idea to have a day here to talk about friends and family who are gone. They have tennis courts, but I only played once. 32 degrees for a guy with extremely white skin, is too much for any sort of physical activity. Anyway, I stayed nicely away from any Jays news, not that there was much. And, though I brought my computer, I only turned it on once, because my wife wanted to look up something. Of course I saw the Anthony Santander comments. My personal feeling is that if you are being paid more money than God, and you have had 34 hits over two seasons, don’t say anything that gets your employer paying lawyers to search through your contract to see if it can be voided for stupidity. I’m being paid far less than God, and I’m sure if I posted something as dumb as he did, SB would fire me (very rightfully) in ten seconds. If it were up to me, I’d likely release Anthony now and eat the money. But I’d imagine the team will see how spring training goes. I did see a comment saying we should bring in Shari Lewis law. Everyone has to wear a sock puppet and sing that annoying song on and on. That I’m all for. A question for the Jays is: Do they give the players any media training? Could they maybe do a better job of it? No Jays players won a Gold Glove (I figured Vlad would), but we won the Team Gold Glove, which, around midseason, I would have said had no chance. But looking at the numbers, it does seem earned. This is the third time the Jays have won this award. Lazaro Estrada was signed to a minor league deal. Also Adrian Pinto, Hedbert Perez, Josh Stephan, Geovanny Planchart and Alexis Hernandez have been signed to minor league deals. Jake Bloss has been given another option year. Sometimes players get an extra option year if they use all three in their first five seasons of professional ball. Tonight we learn who the Rookie of the Year is in each league. Tomorrow Manager of the Year.

item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have a captaincy problem, and judging by the latest reactions on social media, some fans are running out of patience with how the organization is handling it. With former captain Dylan Larkin no longer wearing the “C” following his offseason trade request, Detroit has chosen, according to Todd McLellan , to move forward without naming a replacement. The organization previously announced that a permanent decision would be left to its next hockey operations leader, but that approach is drawing criticism from fans who believe the answer is already standing in the Red Wings’ locker room. item.description: BYU guard Delaney Gibb (11) dribbles past Missouri's Shannon Dowell during the Cougars' matchup with the Tigers in the second round of the Women's Basketball Invitation Tournament at the Marriott Center in Provo, Utah, on Monday, March 23, 2026. | Brandon Judd, Deseret News Three games into her junior campaign , Delaney Gibb may have notched her most impressive all-around performance at BYU to date. The Cougars’ star point guard recorded a triple-double Saturday with 15 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists against Montana, marking the program’s first triple-double since 1986. “It looked like a fun game to play in, and then we had an amazing individual statistical night from our point guard,” BYU coach Lee Cummard said postgame. “I can’t believe that it’s been 40 years since we had a triple-double, but that’s pretty cool.” ⭐️First BYU Triple-Double since 1986⭐️ pic.twitter.com/PBvrjHhDCJ — BYU Women's Hoops (@byuwbb) November 7, 2026 Prior to Gibb, the last BYU triple-double that included 10 or more assists rather than blocks came in 1982. Gibb’s 10 assists are a new career high, and it was the fourth time she’s ever grabbed at least 10 rebounds, even doing so in BYU’s previous outing against Portland. “I think I focused a lot on rebounding, just these past couple games because I feel like shooting will come, so I think that’s kind of what fueled it tonight,” Gibb said. “I just have to give thanks to my teammates, they came in clutch and knocked down big-time shots.” Led by Gibb’s efforts, BYU is 3-0 on the young season, having won three games in five days this past week. Gibb is averaging 19 points, nine rebounds and five assists per game, shooting 36% from 3-point range as well. item.title: Fantasy Football Managers Need to Sell Jameson Williams Amid Inconsistent Role
item.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) makes a catch during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jameson Williams is an exciting wideout who generates chunk plays through the air for the Detroit Lions. However, even after a quiet Week 9 performance against the Miami Dolphins, Williams is a sell-high candidate in fantasy football entering Week 10. Let's take a look at Williams' production this season and discuss why fantasy football managers should sell him because of his inconsistent role. All stats used in this article are from PFF and Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros . Fantasy Recap of Jameson Williams After Week 9 Despite scoring a season-low 5.0 fantasy points in Week 9, Williams is still the WR22 in fantasy points per game (13.2). Williams posted 16-plus fantasy points in four straight starts before his dud against the Dolphins. Since Week 4, Williams is the WR14 in fantasy points per game (16.6). Jameson Williams first three games: 7.6 FPTS per game Jameson Williams last four games: 19.5 FPTS per game pic.twitter.com/YWHsahopTm - FantasyPros (@FantasyPros) November 5, 2026 Of the 76 WRs with 25-plus targets this season, Williams has the sixth-most yards per reception (16.7) and the sixth-most receiving touchdowns (5) on the second-highest average depth of target (16.2). Williams continues to operate as the primary vertical threat in Detroit's aerial attack. Buy, Sell, Or Hold Verdict: Sell Jameson Williams Although Williams does possess a decent ceiling, his role isn't one to trust in fantasy football unless an injury occurs to Amon-Ra St. Brown. Williams has just the 54th-highest target share (17.1%) at the WR position. Similar to recent seasons, Williams is dependent on connecting with Jared Goff on explosive plays and finding the end zone. That sort of profile is better for a best-ball format rather than in season-long formats where managers have to set lineups each week. Even with Williams not performing well against the Dolphins, some managers may still be interested in the big-play receiver due to the fact that he's part of an elite offensive environment on the Lions. With Williams having a productive stretch of fantasy points in recent weeks, this is an ideal time to trade him elsewhere. item.title: Nearly 7 months after tragedy, scholarship launched in memory of Jessi Pierce
item.description: Nearly seven months after the tragic deaths of Minnesota sports media personality Jessi Pierce and her three children, a scholarship in her name has been established to support young women pursuing careers in sports journalism. Pierce, whose legal name is Jessi Hinrichs, died along with her children, Hudson, 8, Cayden, 6, and Avery, 4, and the family dog at their home in White Bear Lake on March 21. In September, the State Fire Marshal revealed that the fire was “accidental and electrical in nature, caused by overheating electrical equipment in that office.” On Monday, SKOR North and the Minnesota Broadcasters Foundation launched the Jessi Pierce Memorial Scholarship. Pierce was the Minnesota Wild correspondent for NHL.com and a regular contributor at SKOR North, while also co-hosting the “Bardown Beauties” podcast with Kirsten Krull. “Jessi was loved not only by those who knew her personally, but by sports fans around the state of Minnesota and the world,” said SKOR North’s Phil Mackey. “Her personality was infectious and she brought great joy to all who knew her. It is our hope that this scholarship will continue to shine a light on Jessi’s remarkable life while helping young women grow in the journalism profession.” The goal is to fund the scholarship and continue it into the future. Fundraising efforts will include a weeklong radiothon-style fundraiser via SKOR North’s podcasts and Minnesota Hockey’s Jessi Pierce Community Cup , a youth girls’ hockey tournament that’ll debut Dec. 11-13 at TRIA Rink in St. Paul. “Jessi was passionate about women’s role in sports journalism. We believe this scholarship will contribute to her legacy,” said Dan Seeman, Hubbard Broadcasting’s regional president. The scholarship has already received donations from the Wild and Blaze Credit Union, and you can donate right here . item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Jamari Johnson #9 of the Oregon Ducks scores a rushing touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Ohio State Buckeyes at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. A season that began more or less according to expectations, despite the (survivable) second-half meltdown at Texas, has become an unthinkable mess in the wake of an injury to Julian Sayin and Matt Patricia’s defense falling apart. Let’s sift through the wreckage of the latest disaster, a 41-28 home loss to Oregon and a second consecutive defeat despite an early 14-0 lead. Arthur Smith’s play calling shows lack of awareness Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith seems to have no understanding of his personnel. The game’s opening play was an end around for Devin McCuin that relied on tight end blocking on the left side. Mason Williams, like so many of Keenan Bailey’s underperforming tight ends, could not effectively carry out the assignment. McCuin was dropped for a one-yard loss. Late in the second quarter, it was a failed Bennett Christian block that allowed a swing pass to Bo Jackson to be dropped for a loss of three. Someone else has to answer for the poor blocking in a position group that is tasked with so much vital blocking, but it’s Smith’s job to know what his personnel can and can’t do. Smith also doesn’t seem to understand his backup quarterback, pressed into becoming a freshman starter, isn’t 6-foot-5; he’s listed at 5-foot-11, so he’s probably a little under that. item.title: Christian McCaffrey surpasses Hall of Famer to set new NFL record
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers scores a second quarter touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday was a case of another week, another record for Christian McCaffrey, only this one was a biggy. McCaffrey had a quiet day in terms of yardage in the 49ers’ 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. He had 87 total scrimmage yards, rushing for 67 on the ground, three fewer than rookie backup Kaelon Black. But he found the endzone twice, giving the 49ers a lead they never relinquished with a short-yardage plunge on the opening drive before scoring on a 12-yard reception in the second quarter. It was the latter touchdown that carried historical significance. McCaffrey’s touchdown reception marked the 37th of his illustrious career and took him ahead of arguably the finest dual-threat running back in the history of the sport. That score saw McCaffrey set the record the most touchdown receptions by a running back in the Super Bowl era, breaking his tie with Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk (36). Like Faulk, McCaffrey is destined to end up in Canton, having established himself as the pre-eminent do-it-all back of his era, his skills as both a runner and a receiver weaponized to an even greater degree in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. Of course, Faulk has the one thing McCaffrey is still chasing, having won Super Bowl XXXIV with the St. Louis Rams. But, having a backup in Black who can lessen the burden on him could be crucial in helping McCaffrey be at his best when it really counts in the postseason as he seeks to finally secure that Super Bowl ring. “We love our room. I think with KB, when he comes in it’s such a spark. When I can come in and come out and get my wind, he goes in, balls out, comes out, gets his wind. If we can just continue to do that, man, I think we can be really special,” McCaffrey said after the win over Las Vegas. “Jordan [James], also another guy who has been working so hard. When he touches the ball, he’s very dangerous as well. We’ve got a super high standard in that room and that’s because we know how good we can be. It’s because of guys like KB, because of guys like JJ and the rest of the guys who continue to push each other.”

item.title: ‘He’s a coward. He can’t coach’: Dave Portnoy demands apology after being ‘right about Ryan Day from the jump’
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It was a rough weekend for Michigan, as the Wolverines lost to rival Michigan State and fired their offensive coordinator. But Barstool Sports founder and devoted Michigan fan Dave Portnoy still found something to celebrate. Ohio State suffered a blowout loss of its own, falling to Oregon for its second straight defeat. And Portnoy, who has been a longtime critic of Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day, said he’s owed an apology from every Ohio State fan in Columbus. Portnoy’s Feud With Ryan Day Portnoy has been one of Day’s harshest critics for years, and things have only gotten more personal this season. In August, he called Day a “scared little chicken-boy” after Ohio State moved its senior day from the Michigan game to Week 1. Then in October, Barstool was removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff , and Portnoy blamed Day for the decision. “I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy sh*t even I didnt realize he was this soft,” Portnoy wrote on X at the time, calling the Buckeyes coach “Cryin Ryan.” Awful Announcing noted that the breakup was always inevitable . A couple of weeks later, Portnoy said that Day “would be unsuccessful at any program other than Ohio State.” “Ryan Day was born on third base,” Portnoy said. “Like, anybody here could coach that team to 10, 11 wins.” This weekend gave Portnoy plenty of new material. Michigan fell 15-6 to Michigan State, and the Wolverines fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, whom Portnoy had called “horrific.” But Ohio State blew a 14-0 lead in a 41-28 loss to Oregon, its second straight defeat, and Day said afterward that “there needs to be accountability” for the team’s struggles. ‘He’s a coward’ On Monday’s episode of Wake Up Barstool , Portnoy made it clear that he was enjoying Ohio State’s struggles. “I want an apology from every single person in Columbus. I want them to get in line and line up,” Portnoy said, in a clip shared by the show . “I want them all to come in a receiving line and say, ‘Hey, Dave Portnoy, you’ve been right about Ryan Day from the jump. He’s a coward. He can’t coach. He was born on third base.’ All of it. Get in line and say, ‘I’m sorry, you should be back on Big Noon Kickoff . It was a joke what they did to you,'” he continued. Portnoy admitted that Michigan has problems of its own, but he said that Ohio State’s situation is even worse given the talent on the roster. “Yes, we have problems in Ann Arbor, but that team’s a joke with the talent they have. So yeah, real bad weekend for Michigan, no doubt,” Portnoy said. “But let’s not forget, as bad as a weekend Michigan had, Michigan State had a worse weekend, and Ohio State had the worst weekend of the bunch.” Needless to say, Portnoy is going to enjoy every minute of this before The Game. item.description: EAST HARTFORD, CONNECTICUT - NOVEMBER 07: Trey Blue #77 of the North Carolina Tar Heels reacts following the NCAA college football game against the Connecticut Huskies at Pratt & Whitney Stadium on November 07, 2026 in East Hartford, Connecticut. (Photo by Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two amazingly close games for the Tar Heels, both losses, and then a trip up to New England in the fall could have spelled disaster for Carolina. The setup is one that many teams have fallen victim to before, and honestly one that last year’s Tar Heels would have tripped up on. To get yourself back up after the loss to Syracuse and play that game against Miami, just for it to fall short, leads to a lot of teams just being done with the season. There was at least a little bit of that in the first quarter for the Tar Heels, but some good defense got the ball rolling, and then the offense found the form it had discovered last week. The defense also found a bit of its form, but this time UConn wasn’t Miami, and the Tar Heels are one win away from bowl eligibility with three games left. Let’s look at the winners, losers, and honorable mentions from the Tar Heels’ 38-21 dominating win over the Huskies. Winners Jelani Thurman- If there is one positive that came out of last weekend it was Thurman’s work on such a big stage, and hopefully it captured the attention of the John Mackey Award committee. Should they be watching, they’ll have seen yet another stellar effort from the Ohio State transfer. You also have to wonder if, after Ohio State’s embarrassing loss to Oregon on Saturday, Thurman is having more fun in Chapel Hill, even with the lower stakes. His seven catches for 64 yards and two touchdowns led the team, and despite now being enough of a focus to face specialized coverage, he still can get his hands on the ball. Just an amazing find in the portal, and it’s going to cost a lot of money to keep him from going to the NFL. Benjamin Hall- Welcome back, Benjamin. He was seen a little last weekend against Miami and now he showed off how healthy he is for this final stretch of the season. item.description: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 01: Trea Turner #7 of the Philadelphia Phillies looks on from the dugout prior to Game Three of the National League Wild Card Series presented by AbbVie between the Philadelphia Phillies and the Atlanta Braves at Truist Park on Thursday, October 1, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Rob Tringali/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images While these report cards are about looking back on someone’s season, it doesn’t entirely seem right in Trea Turner’s case. There was no injury or excuse for why he had the worst season of his career but the format for how we do these report cards doesn’t seem right. Here is one way to look at it: Trea Turner has seven more years on his contract, with an average annual value over $27 million. He will enter his age 33/34 season in 2027 and is coming off the worst season of his career. The Phillies are still going to treat him like he’s a star player. He will play shortstop in 2027, albeit on thin ince . He will probably bat at the top of the lineup for most, if not all, of 2027 unless multiple players perform much better than him. So instead of purely discussing what went right or wrong in 2026, the goal will be to put it all into context for what 2027 could look like. Is this a pure outlier? Is he cooked? The answer is probably somewhere in the middle. 2026 stats: 157 games, .242/.297/.378, .675 OPS, 15 home runs, 58 RBIs, 21 SBs, 21.0% K%, 6.9% BB%, 83 wRC+, 1.1 fWAR What went right Not a lot of things went right for Trea Turner but the physical markers are not in a terrible spot. He still ranks in the 98th percentile for sprint speed and he probably stole as many bases as he could with an on-base percentage below .300 and their two best hitters right after him for most of the season. His 90th percentile exit velocity is roughly similar to his past at 103.6 mph, although a tick lower than in 2025. His bat speed looked normal as well. So the general surface-level physical markers we can use are not indicating he is physically cooked, at least not yet, but it doesn’t entirely tell the full story for him at the plate. What went wrong Trea Turner went from being good at making contact against velocity to not being good at it. His whiff rate against pitches 95+ jumped three ticks. His whiff rate against secondary pitches jumped over two ticks and his zone contact rate dropped roughly two ticks. This all happened with Turner’s pull fly ball rate not spiking so it wasn’t like he was trying to sell out for power either. This is not some easy fix for anyone involved and why we should be very skeptical on 2026 being a complete outlier. He just might not be as good at making contact anymore. Defensively is where a lot of concerns about 2026 will apply to 2027, at least initially. Trea Turner is going to be their shortstop to start next season. item.description: Nov 14, 2015; Tucson, AZ, USA; Arizona Wildcats mascot Wilbur surfs the crowd as students rush the field after defeating the Utah Utes at Arizona Stadium. Arizona won 37-30 in double overtime. Mandatory Credit: Casey Sapio-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect November is one of the best months in Tucson. The weather has finally cooled down, college basketball has begun and the biggest college town in America lives up to that billing. But for many visiting ranked football teams, November is a month they’d like to avoid. When the UA hosts No. 2 Utah on Saturday evening at Casino Del Sol Stadium it will be the 38 th time a Top 25 opponent has come to town in November. Fourteen of those have left with a loss, including nine who were ranked in the Top 10. It’s been seven years since a Top 10 team came to Tucson in November, that being Utah in 2019 when it was ranked 7 th and rolled to a 35-7 win. But the previous five Top 10 visitors got knocked off by the Wildcats, including 10th-ranked Utah in double overtime in 2015 and Top 5 Oregon squads in 2013 and 2007. The 2007 win over No. 2 Oregon was the last time Arizona hosted a Top 2 team. The Wildcats were 4-6 and headed towards a ninth straight bowl-less season but they scored 21 straight points—including interception and punt return touchdowns by Antoine Cason— to build a 31-11 halftime lead and then held on to win 34-24. The Oregon win was the third of three Top 5 wins at home in November in as many seasons. In 2006 Cason had a game-winning pick-6 to beat No. 8 California, and in 2005 the UA steamrolled unbeaten No. 7 UCLA 52-14. Before that you have to go back to 1992 for a November home win over a Top 10 team, and it was the biggest of them all. Arizona was playing its second top-ranked opponent of the season, losing 8-7 at Miami in September, but when unbeaten Washington brought its 22-game win streak to Arizona Stadium the Wildcats weren’t going to miss out on a second chance to take out No. 1. Thanks to four takeaways, the UA beat the Huskies 16-3. Overall, Arizona is 31-65 at home against ranked opponents, the most recent being last season when No. 6 BYU won in double OT. The last home win over a ranked team was in 2023, a 42-18 blowout of No. 16 Utah on Senior Day.

See the post below. “Soon 2027,” Rakhmonov wrote, along with a clenched fist emoji. Rakhmonov appears to be responding to rumors that circulated on social media over the weekend concerning his health, with unconfirmed reports claiming his ongoing battle with knee injuries hit another bump and that he would not be fighting again anytime soon. While Rakhmonov’s statement doesn’t guarantee anything, he at least appears to be gearing up for a return. The undefeated Rakhmonov (19-0) most recently fought at UFC 310 in December 2024, where he defeated Ian Machado Garry, who stepped in as a replacement for injured welterweight champion Belal Muhammad. Rakhmonov’s win all but guaranteed him the next crack at Muhammad, but injuries have kept Rakhmonov out of competition and Muhammad later dropped the title to Jack Della Maddalena who subsequently lost it to Islam Makhachev. item.title: Michael Carrick’s atrocious handling of United’s best defender is another reason he should be sacked
item.description: Michael Carrick’s atrocious handling of United’s best defender is another reason he should be sacked Manchester United could have handled Matthijs de Ligt ’s return from injury far better, and Arsenal have just shown them exactly how with William Saliba. For those who have followed the game for any length of time, the approach used to be standard across most clubs: players returning from injury built their match fitness with the reserves. Louis van Gaal even employed the method with Memphis Depay and Marouane Fellaini during his time at Old Trafford. In recent years, however, that sensible practice has largely disappeared. Clubs now routinely throw players straight back into first-team action. The results are predictable and costly: re-injuries occur more frequently, and those who avoid further setbacks often take far longer to rediscover their form because they lack proper match sharpness. United cannot afford to overlook these small but crucial details in player rehabilitation if they genuinely intend to compete. They would do well to take note of what their rivals are doing. Saliba finding his match fitness with the Arsenal under-21s Arsenal’s Saliba , who picked up an injury at the World Cup, has not been rushed back into the first team. Instead, the Gunners sent him to their under-21s to regain match fitness. The Frenchman played 45 minutes in Arsenal Under-21s’ 5-2 win over Aston Villa. Another two or three appearances at that level should have him fully ready to return to a first-team starting role. The same measured approach is evident lower down the pyramid. Peterborough United centre-back Sam Hughes spent 15 months on the sidelines with an Achilles injury. When he returned, the club did not throw the 29-year-old straight into senior football. They handed him three games with the under-21s first, allowing him to build fitness properly before rejoining the first-team squad. De Ligt injury return handled poorly If Arsenal and even Peterborough can manage returns this way, why has De Ligt not been given similar opportunities with United’s under-21s? He managed 79 minutes against Como but has barely featured since, despite clear evidence that he still needs competitive minutes to rediscover full match fitness. Regular under-21 appearances would have given him that platform without unnecessary risk. Had United taken this route, starting him against Liverpool would not feel like such a gamble, especially with Harry Maguire now carrying a back injury after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, which means the Dutch defender might have to start. United need to change how they handle players returning from long-term injuries. Getting these details right could alter the team’s entire dynamic. Before his injury, De Ligt had established himself as the Red Devils’ best defender. Properly prepared through under-21 football, he could have returned looking every bit like a new signing.

item.title: Cubs free agent target: Trevor Rogers
item.description: Here’s a left-hander who hasn’t been mentioned much in connection with the Cubs, but I think Trevor Rogers might actually be a very good fit as a free agent starting pitcher. Rogers had a bumpy start to his career with the Marlins, missing quite a bit of time due to injuries, including a lat strain which cost him most of the 2023 season. He’s been mostly healthy since the Orioles acquired him at the deadline in 2024 for Connor Norby and Kyle Stowers, a rare trade that helped both teams. Rogers made a career-high 30 starts in 2026 and posted a 4.03 ERA and 1.185 WHIP, a 2.2 bWAR season that registered lower on the WAR scale than his 2025 (5.3 bWAR with a 1.81 ERA in 18 starts). While overall his 2026 numbers don’t look that great, they were skewed by some pretty bad outings in May. From June 1 to season’s end Rogers posted a 2.90 ERA (2.89 FIP) and 1.033 WHIP in 20 starts covering 121 innings, a large enough sample size to perhaps indicate that 2025 was not a fluke. He doesn’t walk guys (5.6 percent walk rate) and generally keeps the ball in the ballpark (19 home runs in 169.2 innings). He’s got a more or less traditional pitch mix: Rogers turns 29 on Friday. MLB Trade Rumors has him at five years, $115 million and The Athletic says four years, $84 million, basically the same AAV of $21 million. Seems worth it to me. What do you think?

item.description: UNITED STATES - MARCH 30: College Basketball: NCAA Final Four, Indiana Keith Smart (23) in action, making game winning, buzzer beating shot vs Syracuse Howard Triche (25), New Orleans, LA 3/30/1987 (Photo by Jerry Wachter/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (SetNumber: X34597) A new chapter in the battle between the Syracuse Orange men’s basketball team and the Indiana Hoosiers will be written Monday night. Many in Upstate New York remember the first. “Smart takes the shot. OHH! And the Hoosiers with three seconds go ahead!” Nearly 40 years ago, both squads met on the court for the first time in New Orleans. It was the 1987 NCAA Championship, the first one for Syracuse under legendary head coach Jim Boeheim. True Orange fans remember the names that almost got the program its first title: Sherman Douglas, Rony Seikaly, Derrick Coleman . Well, almost. Because on the other side of the court were the Hoosiers and Keith Smart’s heroics. Decades later, “The Shot” is still one of the most iconic plays in college basketball history. And unfortunately, Syracuse was on the receiving end of it. Since then, quite a lot has happened between the two programs. Now, both find themselves in similar situations entering Monday’s game. Syracuse returned to the NCAA Championship game in 1996, before Boeheim and the Orange finally captured their first and only title in 2003. Syracuse then rode some memorable highs (and lows) as the Boeheim era eventually came to an end. After Smart’s shot, Indiana has never been back. The Hoosiers had their own legendary coach, Bob Knight. He remained on the sidelines for 13 more seasons, but Indiana only got as far in March Madness as the Elite Eight (and just once after ‘87). After Knight left, there have been glimpses of the “old Indiana”: 2002 under Mike Davis, 2013 with Tom Crean, and even a pair of improved years this decade with Mike Woodson. But it wasn’t the same, much like how Syracuse had some good “surprise” seasons (2016 and 2021), even if things were clearly not what they once were. Syracuse and Indiana don contrasting colors, yet share much of the same story: two historic programs that have been around forever, searching for answers that will get them back to the mountaintop. Syracuse hasn’t reached the NCAA Tournament since 2020-21 under Boeheim. After his weird but eventual exit, the program just couldn’t remotely return to form under Adrian Autry. Now, it’s Gerry McNamara’s turn. As for Indiana, it’s made the tournament twice in the last decade. Since Crean’s departure, the Hoosiers are now on their third coach, Darian DeVries. Monday will mark an important step for both sides if this season truly is “the one.” First Power Five non-conference clash for either team. First true test of 2026-27.
